scenario.name: r-cd-token-bracket-delegate
scenario.description: Terminal [[CONTINUE_DELEGATE:...]] path from an isolated raw-final-text child; joins a runner-owned attempt to exactly one origin task, one structurally owned token-scheduled delegate, completion, return, and Tempo topology.
scenario.registryNotes: Issue #426/#517 runnable repair: runner owns the attempt/nonce before launch; the unlabeled token task is correlated by the unique disposable origin-child requester lineage and optional parentTaskId, never title prose.

seatClassExpectation.reason: Bracket scanner fires only on scanned-final-text. Seats that route final-text through message(send) body cannot prove this row and remain PARTIAL unless raw-final-text mode is forced (no message-tool call that turn). See TOOLS.md bracket-position-sensitive notes.

review.notes: Bracket/token path. Message-body delivery cannot prove this contract and remains PARTIAL-candidate. PASS-candidate requires a raw-final-text seat. candidateSha and seat resolve from env at runtime.

census.limits: This is the row the census bites hardest. Its whole claim is that the delegate came from a bracket token and not from a typed tool, and it proves that today by the ABSENCE of a typed continue_delegate tool origin in the trace. The census established that accepted entry spans carry no origin and that typed-tool spans and accepted-entry spans cannot be causally joined, so absence-of-a-tool-span is a heuristic, not a positive origin proof. Bracket origin currently has positive evidence only in payload-free Loki effective-signal logs (32 bracket-delegate records in 7d), which are not bound to the trace.

spans.name: openclaw.tool.execution
spans.notes: Its ABSENCE is the current bracket-origin heuristic.

attributes.notes: Emitted today and already asserted by the row’s trace-correlation resolver. It is the strongest join currently available and it is not an identity.
raw-final-text | message-tool-body | typed-tool. The row’s seat-class expectation is exactly this distinction and no span records it.
Accepted entry spans carry no signal.kind on the census product basis; origin is contracted by R-OBS-CONT-PROVENANCE.
No k6/Project-81 resource or trace marker exists, so this row’s traffic cannot be separated from organic fleet traffic in a later census.

redaction.rule: Delegate task material is published as a digest and a length. The bracket text, the origin child’s final text, raw nonces, session keys, and tokens never enter the artifact.

controls.positive: A disposable raw-final-text origin child emits the terminal bracket, exactly one token-scheduled delegate task identity appears in the authoritative ledger, it completes, and the nonce-bound return sentinel reaches the parent.
controls.negative: A message-tool-body surface cannot satisfy the row and stays PARTIAL-candidate; a typed continue_delegate tool origin in the same trace disqualifies the bracket claim; more than one nonce-bound delegate identity through the settle window fails the row.
controls.notes: The negative control is currently an absence test. R-OBS-CONT-PROVENANCE converts it into a positive origin assertion.

backendUnavailable.notes: A degraded backend cannot support an absence argument at all: with no completeness metadata, "no typed tool span" and "no data" are the same response. Backend-partial therefore caps this row at PARTIAL-candidate without exception.

verdictAuthority.pass: A runner-owned attempt on a raw-final-text seat with exactly one origin task and one token-scheduled delegate task, exact completion and return binding, and public Tempo topology. Behavioral only: bracket origin is established by surface declaration plus tool-span absence, not by a product origin attribute.
verdictAuthority.partial: Message-body or unknown surfaces, interruption, or a degraded/partial telemetry backend. None of these are auto-retried.
verdictAuthority.fail: More than one nonce-bound delegate identity, a typed continue_delegate tool origin in the row trace, or a missing return binding.

execution.deterministicK6: r-cd-token-bracket-delegate.js with a runner-owned attempt and nonce established before k6 launches.
execution.manual: Manual bracket fires cannot bound the origin surface and are not admissible for this row.
execution.relationship: Deterministic k6 is the sole authority here precisely because the origin claim is an absence argument that needs a bounded, owned window.

liveRunSafety.notes: PASS requires a runner-owned attempt, disposable raw-final-text origin, exactly one origin task and one token-scheduled delegate task through a settle window, exact completion/return binding, and public Tempo topology. Message-body/unknown surfaces and interruption are structured PARTIAL and never auto-retried.
